chunks: Whoever performs hajj on behalf of another should say: “O Allah, whatever hardship, fatigue, or dishevelment has afflicted me, then reward so-and-so for it, and reward me in my carrying it out on his behalf.”

And it has been narrated: “He mentions him when he slaughters. If he does not say anything, then there is nothing upon him, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows what is hidden. Whoever gives a hajj or an umrah to a relative, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, writes for him two hajj and two umrahs. Likewise, whoever carries it out on behalf of a close friend, the reward is multiplied twofold for him.”

key_terms.اَللَّهُمَّ: O Allah; opening of the supplication
key_terms.حَمِيمٍ: a close friend or intimate companion
key_terms.شَعَثٍ: dishevelment and untidy condition from travel and worship
key_terms.غَيْرِهِ: another person on whose behalf the rite is performed
key_terms.قَضَائِي: my fulfillment or discharge of the act

ai.seo_question: What should a person say when performing hajj on behalf of someone else, and is naming them during sacrifice required?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the supplication and etiquette for one who performs hajj on behalf of another person. It also states that naming the person at the time of sacrifice is narrated as recommended, while omission brings no liability because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows hidden intentions, and it highlights multiplied reward for gifting hajj or umrah to relatives and close companions.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2244 - Whoever performs Hajj on behalf of another should say: "O Allah (swt), whatever hardship, fatigue, or dishevelment I experience, reward so-and-so for it and reward me for fulfilling it on their behalf."

It has also been narrated: "They should mention the name of the person on whose behalf they are performing the Hajj when they slaughter the sacrificial animal. However, if they do not say anything, there is no blame upon them, for Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, knows all that is hidden."
Whoever gifts a Hajj or Umrah to a relative, Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, records for them the reward of two Hajj and two Umrah. Likewise, whoever performs Hajj or Umrah on behalf of a close friend, their reward is doubled.
